transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-03-04 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Recording: automated
Attendees: Evan Morales (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Marcus Liu (Redwood CSM), Ana Petrova (Redwood SE); Lydia Chen (NovaQuartz Head of ML), Marco Ruiz (Infra), Sarah Owens (Finance), Ben Hall (SRE), Olivia Park (Product)

Summary (auto): Kickoff to scoping a 6-week POC focused on unit economics and latency budget. Discussed per-token targets, batching and KV caching knobs, benchmark plan, and timeline. Action items captured.

Transcript: 
[00:00] Evan (Redwood AE): hey everybody, thanks for joining, appreciate you making time. quick round‑robin intros?
[00:08] Lydia (NovaQuartz): hi yes Lydia, head of ML at NovaQuartz, we've been working on recommendation rerank and a small chat assistant for ops.
[00:15] Marco (Infra): Marco, infra, i'll share traces after.
[00:18] Sarah (Finance): Sarah from finance, i'm mainly here for runway questions and cost guardrails.
[00:23] Evan: great. so goal for today's call — align on POC success criteria, workload sizing, and our benchmark plan so we can give per‑token estimates and a realistic budget.
[00:32] Priya (Redwood SE): i'll drive the technical bits — typical knobs we'll look at: batching window, prefix/K V cache reuse, quantized model variants, and routing to lower-cost model fallbacks. quick note: K V cache sometimes shows up in transcripts as K V cash, so if you see odd words in the export ignore that.
[00:48] Ben (SRE): quick question — we need private deployment? data residency concerns?
[00:52] Lydia: some PII in logs, but initial POC can run hosted with strict retention if we can guarantee no logs persisted beyond 30 days. our security team will need SOC2/ISO statement.
[01:02] Evan: that's doable; we'll include SOC2 docs and a KMS/HSM integration note.
[01:06] Olivia (Product): and timeline? we have a quarterly milestone in 8 weeks so ideally POC done before then.
[01:12] Evan: we recommend a 4–6 week POC; given your milestone let's aim 6 weeks to leave room for bench iteration.
[01:18] Sarah: cost-wise: our runway allows ~$60k for this pilot. want to know what that buys us.
[01:25] Priya: fair. to translate that into SLOs we need: concurrent qps, avg prompt size, avg completion length, and reuse rate for caching. can you share numbers?
[01:34] Marco: baseline: peak concurrent 45 qps, typical 15 qps, 95th percentile bursts up to 70 qps for 90s windows. prompt size average 120 tokens, completion average 220 tokens.
[01:46] Priya: ok that helps. quick back‑of‑envelope: per‑request tokens ~340, at 15 qps sustained that's ~5.1k tokens/sec ~15.4M tokens/hour. multiply by 8 hours daily — big numbers. but with batching and KV cache reuse for chat flows we can cut effective token compute significantly.
[02:07] Lydia: when you say cut, what's realistic? 2x? 5x?
[02:10] Priya: depends — for a rerank flow with short prompts we often see 3–6x effective cost reduction via batching + prefix reuse; for full chat with long completions it's usually 1.5–3x. we'll benchmark to get exact numbers.
[02:23] Evan: important to define success criteria — Lydia, Sarah, what matters to you?
[02:27] Lydia: accuracy/quality on our golden prompt set must be within 2% of our baseline (we'll provide evals). also p95 latency under 200ms for rerank and under 800ms for chat completions.
[02:38] Sarah: and cost per 1M tokens target — less than $X? we're open to Redwood's estimate.
[02:43] Evan: we'll produce per‑token estimates for hosted vs reserved capacity; initial ballpark for hosted using open 13B quantized model is around $25–40 per 1M tokens depending on batching; dedicated reserved can push down to $12–20/1M with sustained throughput and autoscaling. we'll validate during bench.
[02:59] Marco: question on burst handling — if we have a spike to 70 qps, will Redwood autoscale automatically or do we need reserved burst capacity?
[03:06] Priya: autoscaling works but there's cold‑start latency for new instances; recommended pattern: base reserved capacity for steady-state and reserve burst pool (dedicated or pre-warmed) for spikes. we can model cost tradeoffs in the pricing worksheet.
[03:18] Ana (Redwood): also consider model routing — route non-critical traffic to lower-cost variant automatically when capacity is constrained.
[03:24] Ben: and what about KV cache eviction on long chat sessions? does it survive model variant switches?
[03:30] Priya: KV cache is tied to model family and tokenization; when switching to a compatible variant we can reuse cache, but switching to a smaller architecture loses some reuse. we'll simulate both in bench runs.
[03:40] Lydia: ok on the bench — what's the plan?
[03:44] Priya: step 1: we request a 5k golden prompt sample from you — representative of rerank + chat. step 2: we run three model variants (13B quantized, 34B half, 34B quant with int8 path) across three concurrency profiles (steady 15 qps, peak 45 qps, burst 70 qps short). step 3: capture p50/p95/p99 latencies, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, and per‑1M token cost under different batching windows (10ms, 50ms, 200ms) and prefix cache hit rates (0%, 40%, 70%). we'll then produce a dashboard and recommendations.
[04:23] Lydia: sample size? you said 5k.
[04:25] Priya: yes, 5k prompts total across flows; it's small but gives statistically useful signals. ideally one of your engineers annotates 200 golden cases for quality gating.
[04:34] Olivia: what's the expected duration of the bench runs?
[04:37] Priya: bench runs take ~24–48 hours for full matrix but we'll prioritize short smoke tests first and then a full run.
[04:43] Sarah: and how will cost be reported? raw per‑token, plus amortized infra and caching impact?
[04:48] Evan: we'll show both raw per‑token inference cost and end‑user per‑request cost factoring in batching effect, KV hit rate, and routing to fallbacks. we'll also model reserved vs hosted pricing options for the POC period.
[04:59] Marco: can you show an example calculation now?
[05:02] Priya: sure — say average request 340 tokens. If unbatched per‑token cost is $0.00004 (that's $40/1M) then per request cost = 340 * 0.00004 = $0.0136. If batching achieves 3x effective improvement, the effective per request cost becomes ~$0.0045. Over 15 qps sustained that becomes roughly $2.3k/day — rough numbers.
[05:26] Sarah: that math is helpful. with $60k runway over 6 weeks (~42 days) that's about $1.4k/day budget — suggests we need better than 3x or go reserved.
[05:35] Priya: exactly the tradeoff. reserved can cut unit cost in half for steady load but has commit. for a short POC we sometimes recommend hybrid: hosted for flexibility + small reserved base for steady traffic.
[05:46] Lydia: what about caching strategies for rerank? we have many repeated item descriptions, could we cache embeddings?
[05:50] Priya: yes, embeddings cache and rerank cache are huge wins — if you precompute embeddings and cache top candidates, inference cost for rerank is mostly model scoring which can be batched. we'll include an embeddings precompute plan in the worksheet.
[06:03] Ben: security checklist — SSO, SAML, RBAC, audit logs, KMS. any blockers?
[06:08] Evan: Redwood supports SSO/SAML, fine‑grained RBAC, and audit logs. KMS/HSM integration is supported for Private and can be enabled for Dedicated; for Hosted we support customer-managed keys via cloud KMS in many regions. we'll attach a security pack.
[06:21] Lydia: our sec team will want to run a short checklist call. can we schedule?
[06:24] Evan: yes — we'll set that up next week.
[06:26] Ana: one nuance to call out: tokenizer differences across model variants can change token counts by ~5–12%, that impacts per‑token math. we'll normalize tokenization in the bench pipeline.
[06:38] Marco: any precedence on billing for failed responses or retries? we bill on tokens generated; retries will count so we'll aim to make client side backoff and dedupe.
[06:46] Priya: also important — continuous batching has a latency vs cost knob. for sub‑200ms p95 SLOs we usually keep batching window under 50ms; that reduces cost savings versus larger windows.
[06:56] Lydia: for rerank p95 <200ms we need that tight window. for chat <800ms is more forgiving.
[07:02] Evan: noted. we'll target batching config: 30ms for rerank, 100ms for chat, and show tradeoffs.
[07:08] Sarah: can you include a model fallback policy example? if quality delta is within X% route to smaller model automatically?
[07:15] Priya: yes — example policy: if quality metric (NDCG or our eval score) decline <2% then route low-priority traffic to 13B; else keep on 34B. we'll show a canary rollout config.
[07:28] Olivia: timeline recap?
[07:30] Evan: week 0 (this week) — kick off and collect traces and golden prompts. week 1 — smoke benches and pricing worksheet. weeks 2–3 — full bench matrix and optimization runs. week 4 — integrate caching and rerun targeted tests. week 5 — user acceptance quality checks and final cost model. week 6 — wrap, deliver recommendations and decision doc.
[07:54] Lydia: courts — that fits our roadmap.
[07:57] Ben: on instrumentation — what metrics will Redwood publish?
[08:00] Priya: token consumption per route, p50/p95/p99, GPU util, batching window stats, KV cache hit rate, per‑route cost breakouts, and trace sampling for debugging.
[08:12] Marco: can we get raw logs to our S3?
[08:15] Evan: yes, log export to your bucket, with retention controls. for hosted we'll mask PII by default, but you can choose stricter retention.
[08:24] Sarah: anything else from finance — commit options?
[08:27] Evan: we'll present two commercial options: short pilot hosted pricing with consumption billing and a small reserved option for base capacity, and a monthly committed reserved plan with discounted unit rates. numbers in the worksheet.
[08:39] Lydia: quality gating — we'll need automated test harness to run golden prompts each deploy. can Redwood trigger that?
[08:45] Priya: yes we can run continuous evals tied to rollouts and alert on regressions.
[08:49] Olivia: client integration — SDKs, webhooks?
[08:52] Ana: SDKs in python/js, streaming, and webhooks for async jobs. sample code and postman collections will be shared.
[08:59] Lydia: small question — do you support partial token caching for multi‑turn?
[09:03] Priya: yes, prefix caching reuses KV across turns so you don't recompute prefix attention for repeated context. that drives big wins for multi‑turn sessions.
[09:11] Marco: is there a recommended config for a 70 qps short burst pattern?
[09:15] Priya: warm a small pool of pre‑warmed instances sized for 70 qps short bursts, and let autoscaler handle the rest. we'll show cost of keeping that warm pool.
[09:24] Sarah: ok let's talk numbers again — if we need p95 200ms for rerank, and our budget is $60k for 42 days — what's feasible?
[09:31] Priya: initial recommendation: reserve a small base for steady 15 qps (reserved) to get unit savings, and keep hosted for spikes. with batching windows tuned and a 50% KV hit rate we can likely meet $60k, but we'll confirm in bench.
[09:44] Lydia: what are typical KV hit rates you see?
[09:46] Priya: for conversations with strong session stickiness 50–80%; for one‑off queries lower (10–30%). rerank caches can be even higher if items repeat.
[09:56] Evan: ok i think we have everything to move forward — action items captured: Evan share pricing playbook, Priya run bench, Marco provide traces, Lydia finalize golden prompts.
[10:05] Lydia: yep. thanks everyone.
[10:08] Evan: we'll schedule the security call and the bench kickoff. thanks, end.

Notes about transcript: occasional speaker mislabels present (the export has a few Speaker 3/4 swaps). Some technical terms transcribed imperfectly (eg. "K V cash" or "int eight path" instead of int8).
